column1: # Zerocheck kernel compilation, measured 2026-08-24 on an M4 Max, machine idle.
# The zerocheck kernel is generated per chip from that chip's constraint DAG and
# compiled the first time the chip is seen. `SP1_METAL_ZEROCHECK_MAX_NODES`
# (default 16384) is meant to keep chips too large to compile off the GPU.
# It does not work: node count does not predict compile cost. Chips in the
# 7,000-13,000 node band cost about ten minutes to compile, while Global:true at
# 15,196 nodes compiles without trouble in every workload measured here.
# macOS caches the compiled shader against its source, so the cost is one-time
# per program per machine -- but it lands on a user's first proof, which appears
# to hang. Compiling the offending chips buys nothing measurable: keccak's warm
# wall is 2.77 s with them and 2.79-2.85 s without.
